note: Rewritten from Snyder 1926, original in English (Five new termites from Panama and Costa Rica, Proceedings of the Entomological Society of Washington 28(1)). The species was described in 1924 from the soldier, and the alate (morphotype) is recorded here for the first time; the holotype soldier (Cat. No. 28765, U.S. National Museum) and paratypes at Yale (Kirby); the specimens come from the type locality, 11 September 1925 (month 9, day 11). The nymph section only abstracts the few characters contrasted with the alate and soldier, and the full original description of the soldier nymph is not translated sentence by sentence. Figures 1—3 (marginal teeth of the alate mandibles; dorsal and lateral views of the tuberculate area of the soldier nymph) are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate: head dark chestnut brown with a reddish tinge, smooth and shining, with scattered long hairs; compound eyes black, not round, projecting, their distance from the lateral margin of the head less than the long diameter of the eye; ocelli transparent, small, projecting, nearly oval, almost touching the compound eyes; antennae 13-segmented, moniliform; anterior margin of the pronotum broadly and roundly concave, posterior margin nearly straight, sides rounding backwards, the posterior margin bearing a narrow band of raised wrinkled area, longitudinally striate (this area is also visible in the alate nymph); wings dark brown, the costa darker, the wing surface coarsely punctate, the media of the forewing close to and parallel with the subcosta.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark chestnut brown with a reddish tinge, smooth, shining, with scattered long hairs. Compound eyes black, not round, projecting, their distance from the lateral margin of the head less than the long diameter of one eye. Ocelli transparent, small, projecting, nearly oval, almost touching the compound eyes. Antennae pale yellowish brown, 13-segmented, moniliform, lengthening and widening towards the apex; segment 3 slightly shorter than segment 2 but usually slightly longer than segment 4; apical segment slender, nearly half-oval. Pronotum coloured as the head; anterior margin broadly and roundly concave, posterior margin nearly straight, sides rounding backwards; with long hairs; the posterior margin bearing a narrow band of raised wrinkled area, longitudinally striate, this area also visible in the alate nymph. Wings dark brown, the costa darker; wing surface coarsely punctate; media of the forewing close to and parallel with the subcosta; cubitus at about the middle of the wing, giving off branches towards the wing apex and branches and branchlets towards the lower wing margin. Femora of the legs dark chestnut brown, tibiae pale yellow, with 3 dark long spines at the base; with a pulvillus. Abdominal tergites dark chestnut brown, each with a row of long hairs in the middle and a row of shorter hairs at the base; cerci not projecting; styli present in the male. Measurements: total length with wings 7.0—7.5 mm; total length without wings 4.6—4.9 mm; head length (to the tip of the labrum) 1.25—1.3 mm; pronotum length 0.7 mm; forewing length 5.75 mm; hind tibia length 1 mm; long diameter of the compound eye 0.275 mm; head width (at the eyes) 1.1 mm; pronotum width 1 mm; forewing width 1.6 mm.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: Alate nymph: eye spots pink; wing pads fairly long; mesonotum with a rough wrinkled area, but not raised as in the soldier nymph, and brownish rather than pale red; pronotum longer than in the soldier nymph, with a shallower notch. Soldier nymph: mesonotum and median notum with a raised, granulate, tuberculate area (shown in dorsal and lateral view in figures 2 and 3 of the original).
